our_argument_summary: The dome's -6.5 μGal Mohe eclipse gravity anomaly rests on a single marginal LaCoste-Romberg spring-gravimeter reading (Wang et al. 2000), contradicted by (a) the same lead observer's own 2002 reanalysis ('no significant anomaly...was found') and (b) four superconducting gravimeters at the 1999 eclipse (Van Camp et al. 2001) which found nothing above ~0.005 μGal. The 1.67 nT/μGal coupling is a circular ratio (10.9/6.5=1.677) of two hardcoded values validated against itself; verdict 'Not Demonstrated'.

The 'Observed' 1.677 is simply 10.9/6.5 recomputed from two hardcoded eclipse values (BOU 2017 -10.9 nT magnetic; Mohe 1997 -6.5 μGal gravity).

dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: None found. Our detail_evidence's 'κ = 10.9/6.5 = 1.677 ... compares to a hardcoded KAPPA = 1.67 with 5% tolerance. All three values are hardcoded constants' is corroborated by 08-live-power.txt:225.

No external gravimeter fetch. Consistent with c2's monitor.py reading (magnetic_anomaly=10.9, gravity_anomaly=6.5, KAPPA=1.67 baked in).
code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Confirmed correct in current wins.json (c2's MAJOR hole — it was wrongly 'true' — is now fixed). Standard physics does NOT predict an eclipse gravity anomaly; the Allais effect is an unconfirmed 60+yr open question, and SG instruments (Van Camp 2001) found no signal. A WIN claiming a phenomenon standard physics rejects cannot be 'relabeling standard physics'. Now consistent with WIN-013/014 (relabels_standard=false).
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: Wang et al. published the Mohe 1997 reading in 2000 (Phys. Rev. D 62, 041101); the dome (circa 2024) adopted the published value. Not a prospective prediction.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: -6.5 μGal is taken directly from Wang et al. 2000. No dome parameter (disc_radius, H(r), aetheric index) derives it. The dome adopts the observation and labels it confirmed.

holes_found.description: Verdict-tightening question across the WIN-011/012/013/014 group. Our detail_evidence quotes Yang & Wang (2002) — the SAME lead observer as the dome's source — explicitly stating 'no significant anomaly during the very solar eclipse was found', i.e. the original source self-retracts the -6.5 μGal signal. Combined with the four-SG null (Van Camp 2001), the evidence we present is closer to refutation than to 'Not Demonstrated'. WIN-012 (which uses the same -6.5 as κ's denominator) is 'Self-Contradicted' and WIN-013/014 are 'Refuted by Data', so WIN-011 is the softest verdict in a group whose evidence is arguably the most directly retracted by its own author.
holes_found.recommendation: Analyst/decider should consider whether the Yang & Wang 2002 self-retraction plus the four-SG null warrants tightening WIN-011 from 'Not Demonstrated' to 'Refuted by Data' (or 'Self-Contradicted'). Counter-consideration kept deliberately: 'Not Demonstrated' is defensible because a 1997 eclipse cannot be re-measured and a single contested historical reading is more 'unsubstantiated' than 'disproven' — so this is a judgement call, not a clear bug. Not flagging recommended_action=verdict_change for that reason.

holes_found.description: Unsupported quantitative assertions in detail_extra create a tu-quoque vulnerability. We criticise the dome for hardcoded statistics (the 95.2% / r=0.992 / AI=1.152 'hardcoded HTML' pattern), but then assert our own un-shown numbers: 'Monte Carlo simulation shows...' and '37% of red-noise samples with realistic autocorrelation exceed this threshold'. No definition of the Asymmetry Index, no autocorrelation parameter, and no reproducible computation or link is given. A dome defender can say we are doing exactly what we accuse them of — stating a statistic without a visible derivation.
holes_found.recommendation: Either (a) link/cite the Monte Carlo computation (script or notebook) and state the AI definition + AR(1) coefficient used, or (b) soften to a qualitative claim ('during an extreme G5 storm two instruments sharing a massive common environmental driver will exhibit high spurious correlation; an asymmetry index near 1.15 is unremarkable for autocorrelated red noise'). Removing the bare '37%' figure removes the tu-quoque hook.

holes_found.description: Mechanism overstatement in detail_extra: 'any two geophysical instruments respond to the same massive electromagnetic forcing, producing high spurious correlation'. A superconducting gravimeter does not respond directly to nT-scale magnetic forcing — it responds to mass/loading and acceleration. The real source of a spurious magnetometer↔SG-residual correlation during a G5 storm is shared environmental/atmospheric-loading and ionospheric drivers, not a common EM response. The looser 'both respond to EM' phrasing is exploitable.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace 'respond to the same massive electromagnetic forcing' with 'are driven by the same large-scale storm-time environmental forcing (atmospheric/ionospheric loading)' so the spurious-correlation mechanism is physically correct.

stronger_arguments.description: Lead the WIN-011 argument with the source's own self-retraction rather than with Van Camp's different-eclipse null. 'The same lead author (Yang & Wang 2002) found no significant anomaly on reanalysis' is a stronger, harder-to-dodge point than 'a different eclipse in 1999 showed nothing', because it can't be deflected with 'the Allais effect is intermittent / eclipse-geometry-dependent'.

Make explicit that the -6.5 μGal (Mohe 1997) and the -10.9 nT (BOU 2017) come from two different eclipses, two different continents, and two different instruments 20 years apart — so the 'coupling constant' is a cross-event cherry-pick, not a co-measured ratio. This strengthens the circularity point for the WIN-011/012 group.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome correctly identifies that eclipse-time gravity anomalies are a real, published, and still-contested strand of geophysics, not a fabrication (raw-text/02-wins.txt:83-84 cites Wang et al. 2000, a genuine Phys. Rev. D Rapid Communication). The Allais-effect literature (Allais, Saxl & Allen, Wang 2000) does report sub-10 μGal contact-phase anomalies that mainstream geophysics has not fully closed out, so engaging it is not per se pseudoscience.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Granting the literature exists does not validate WIN-011: the specific -6.5 μGal value the dome adopts was self-retracted by its own lead observer (Yang & Wang 2002, per our detail_evidence) and contradicted by four superconducting gravimeters bounding any signal below ~0.005 μGal (Van Camp 2001, verified this run). And the dome never predicts WHEN such anomalies appear or derives -6.5 from dome geometry (code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome=false) — it adopts a contested post-hoc value (post_hoc=true) and feeds it into a self-referential κ check (08-live-power.txt:225 Observed=10.9/6.5). Engaging an open question ≠ confirming a prediction from it.

advocate_mode.best_defense: As a dome defender accepting your six methodological principles: you cannot use a single null at the 1999 eclipse (Van Camp) to refute a phenomenon that the Allais-effect literature describes as INTERMITTENT and eclipse-geometry-dependent. Absence of a signal at one eclipse is not evidence of absence at all eclipses. Wang 2000 is a peer-reviewed Phys. Rev. D result; you are privileging the null and dismissing the positive detection as 'artifact' without proving it was one. By your own 'no default favoritism' principle, you should treat the positive and null detections symmetrically — yet you grant the SG nulls decisive weight while calling the LR detection a 'fluctuation'.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Reframe WIN-011's thrust from 'the phenomenon is debunked' (an overclaim that invites the intermittency rebuttal) to 'the dome's SPECIFIC value is self-retracted and unpredicted'. Concretely: (1) lead with Yang & Wang 2002's self-retraction (same author, same eclipse — intermittency can't rescue it); (2) state plainly that the dome offers no rule for when anomalies occur, so it can't claim predictive success from an intermittent effect; (3) keep Van Camp as corroboration, not as the load-bearing refutation. This makes the symmetry objection moot because we are no longer ruling on the Allais effect in general, only on the dome's adopted number.

cross_win_consistency.inconsistencies_found: No contradiction, but one surface tension worth keeping an eye on: WIN-011 calls the -6.5 μGal 'unconfirmed / Not Demonstrated', while WIN-013/014 APPLY a κ derived from that same -6.5 to predict a 3-9 μGal pulse and then refute the SG nulls. A careless reader could allege 'you can't both dismiss -6.5 as unconfirmed and use it to derive a refuting prediction'. This is already preempted because WIN-013/014's finding text explicitly frames it as 'applying the dome's OWN coupling κ' (i.e. a reductio granting the dome its premise arguendo). Recommend preserving that 'dome's own' wording verbatim wherever κ is applied so the arguendo framing is never lost in a future rewrite.

quantitative_verification.computations: 10.9/6.5 = 1.6769 (matches our stated 1.677). |1.677-1.67|/1.67 = 0.42% < 5% gate (dome's PASS is correct but self-referential). Noise-floor ratio LR(~1 μGal)/SG(~0.001 μGal) = 1000× (matches our '~1,000× more precise'). Van Camp 2001 reported a detection bound of ~0.005 μGal — consistent with our 'found nothing above the instrument noise floor'.

deeper_analysis: Two-cycle spot-check (c2 2026-04-07 -> c3 now). All three of c2's actionable holes are resolved: the MAJOR relabels_standard=true bug is fixed (now false, consistent with WIN-013/014); the MODERATE misplaced GRACE L1A sentence is gone from detail_extra; and the MINOR unverified Van Camp DOI is now verified (four SGs, Aug 11 1999, J. Geod. Soc. Japan article; detection bound ~0.005 μGal). The core argument is sound and the quantitative claims all check out. The two new moderate holes are not factual errors in the central argument but rhetorical/structural exposure: (1) the verdict is the softest in a group whose evidence is arguably the most directly self-retracted, and (2) detail_extra asserts un-shown Monte Carlo statistics that mirror the very 'hardcoded-statistic' pattern we attack in the dome, creating a tu-quoque hook. Advocate mode (rated 3/5) shows the WIN is vulnerable to the 'Allais effect is intermittent, you can't refute it with one null' rebuttal — best neutralised by re-centering on the dome's self-retracted SPECIFIC value rather than litigating the phenomenon in general. recommended_action=minor_edit; current_verdict_holds=true (with the verdict-tightening question logged for analyst/decider judgement).
